name: Burgruine Schrofenstein
kurzbeschreibung: The daring Schrofenstein Castle ruins near Stanz and Landeck cling dramatically to a vertical cliff face high above the Inn Valley.
preis: Free of charge (ruin forecourt and observation point)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round (snow-free months recommended; interior masonry closed for safety)
beschreibung:
Overview

The dramatically positioned Schrofenstein Castle ruins (Burgruine Schrofenstein), perched above the famed distilling village of Stanz near Landeck, rank among Tyrol's most thrilling cliffside castles. Clinging like an eagle's aerie to a sheer rock spur high above the confluence of the Inn and Sanna rivers, the fortress was established in the 12th century. As the ancestral seat of the influential noble Lords of Schrofenstein, this aerie guarded both the ancient Via Claudia Augusta and travel routes toward the Arlberg Pass. Its massive Romanesque keep, standing over twelve metres tall, has withstood centuries of weather and alpine storms. The striking vantage point rewards hikers with staggering vistas across the Landeck valley basin and the surrounding alpine peaks.

Route & Requirements

The trail leading to Burgruine Schrofenstein is a delightful, moderately challenging hike suitable for sure-footed mountain enthusiasts. Starting from the sun-drenched village square of Stanz bei Landeck, a signposted trail ascends steadily through scenic meadows and pine forests in approximately forty-five minutes. The final approach traverses a rocky mountain spine where sturdy hiking boots with grippy soles and basic surefootedness are essential. While the interior of the ancient keep remains closed for safety reasons, the exterior rock terrace is freely accessible and offers a spectacular rest stop.

Visiting & Getting There

Stanz bei Landeck is perched on a sunny plateau just above the district capital of Landeck. From Landeck Hauptbahnhof, frequent local buses climb up to Stanz village centre on weekdays. Drivers will find parking spaces in Stanz village near the community hall. The ruins can be visited freely from spring to late autumn when trails are clear of snow. There is no admission fee.

Tips

Combine your hike with a tasting tour through Stanz, celebrated as Austria's premier distilling village with over sixty active artisan distilleries famed for Stanzer plum schnapps. Experienced hikers can extend the outing along the scenic high trail leading towards Grins or connect with the historic Way of St. James. Do not forget your camera: in late afternoon, warm alpine sunlight bathes the cliffside ruins in golden hues against the rugged Lechtal Alps.
